title: Hit
description: One anagram worth keeping. One line of data/hits.jsonl and one row of the published dataset.

id.description: The candidate id, a colon, and the words sorted and joined with '-'. Two hits with the same words on the same input are the same hit.

words.description: The terms as a multiset, in the order they read best: words of the dictionary as letters, and terms of the labelled classes as their characters (b8, &, 182). A word that carries a leet character is stored as the word (hakes for hake$); the reading says where the character went.

display.description: How the hit reads on Discover: the words in reading order, as themselves or as listed forms (I'm, don't), with apostrophe, hyphen, comma, full stop, question mark, colon, semicolon and quotation marks, and capitals for I, names, acronyms and the start of a sentence; never an exclamation mark. Set by hits:display or from the judge's checked suggestion; hits:order returns it to the words. The tools check it reads exactly the words.

letters.description: The sorted characters (alphagram) the input and the words share, under the hit's reading: letters, and the digits and symbols of the pool.

reading.description: How each digit and symbol of the input is read, every distinct one, keyed by the character (1, 8, 2, $) with the reading name: self (the character is a character of the pool, used by the anagram as itself), a letter (a leet reading: $ as s; the anagram is written with the character where the letter went), or drop (left out). Absent on a hit made before phase N, when every digit and symbol was dropped and the letters kept; the retired hits of 2026-09-21 carry the withdrawn s5 readings and keep their ids. The id and the letters follow the reading either way.

classes.description: The class of each term of the anagram that is not a word of the dictionary, keyed by the term as `words` has it (decision D63): a numeral of the input's digits, a symbol, a shorthand character, a blend, an acronym, a name, a slang word, or the word that carries a leet character (leet). Absent when every term is a word, which is every hit made before the literal phase.

judge.description: One entry per judge, in the shape of the rubric it used: v1 scores aptness, grammar and memorability; v2 scores relation and reads.

tags.description: classic; submitted (from a reader, by the issue form or Build); promoted (a reader promoted it from a search, and the review placed it); alternate (qualified past the per-input cap); greatest-candidate (the judge scored relation 5); note:<text>; shelf:interesting or shelf:stretch (the operator's placement, over the judge's scores); subject:<label>; tone:<label>.

status.description: proposed: not published; an alternate, or waiting for a person. accepted: in the dataset, on Interesting or A stretch. featured: Greatest Hits, set only by the operator. retired: withdrawn; kept so the id is never reused.

justification.description: One plain sentence explaining the link to a reader who does not know the reference. Written by the judge or the operator; the operator can edit it.

about.description: One factual sentence saying what the input is. A copy of the candidate's about, kept the same by every tool that writes either file.

wikipedia.description: The input's English Wikipedia article. A copy of the candidate's wikipedia.

senses.description: The sense a word reads in, in this anagram, keyed by one of the hit's own words. Written only where the dictionary's first sense would not explain the reading, or the word has no definition. The tools check that each key is one of the hit's words.
Senses keyed by word: one sentence of at most 120 characters each.

judged_by.description: Whether the judge routine or a session a person started judged it. Recorded from F0 (2026-09-19) on.

relation.description: How the anagram relates to the input itself; decides the shelf.

reads.description: 3 a phrase someone would say, 2 parses as a headline or list, 1 word salad.

senses.description: The senses the judge proposed for words of the phrase whose first dictionary sense would not explain the reading.

display.description: The display the judge proposed, kept only when it passed the display rule with possessives refused; the hit's display took it when the hit was written.
